workExperience.title: Team Lead

projects.name: 9PP - Yamato Transport
projects.description: Next-generation Android app for collection and delivery field operations, built as a multi-repo, multi-module system (domain / UI layers per business function) with Clean Architecture, MVVM and Jetpack Compose.

roleDetails: Position: Team Lead - own delivery of the FPT-scope functions, coordinate with QC, BA/design and the external platform vendor, and build the AI-driven engineering tooling the team uses daily.
responsibilities: Lead the team delivering 13 business modules (47 functions) across 26+ repositories; split ownership per function, define branch/MR/commit conventions and review gates, and keep the team aligned with QC, BA and vendor-owned components.

Create and review Detail Design for FPT-scope functions, translating business and UI specifications into implementation-ready flows, interface contracts, edge cases and acceptance criteria with BA, QC and the external platform vendor.

Designed and built an AI bug-fixing pipeline on Claude Code (14 skills, 2 agents): scans Jira DC for open bugs, filters out non-actionable tickets, traces root cause across source, design docs and device logs, then routes automatically - in-scope defects get a fix branch + GitLab MR with a root-cause comment; vendor-side defects get a structured Q&A; suspected design errors get a design Q&A and paired design/code MRs.

Integrated the pipeline into Microsoft Teams (Power Automate -> Graph API -> Claude CLI bot) so members trigger tracing, Q&A, resolve, ship and performance-RCA workflows with simple chat commands, with per-command permissions and two-step confirmation for merge/resolve actions.

Built an AI code-review agent for GitLab MRs: reviews each MR against real source, design specs and project-specific rules, comments findings, marks problematic MRs as Draft and tags the responsible owner; auto-fixes small, well-defined issues in AI-authored MRs and re-reviews them.

Created a design-to-code sync agent that reads merged design-document diffs and applies the corresponding UseCase / ViewModel / Screen changes across affected repos, pushing per-repo branches and opening MRs with a self-test report.

Ran cross-function rollouts (TKN) of recurring fixes: inventory script, pilot on one function, then one MR per repo across all modules - covering back-navigation exit handling, navigation-enum unification and resource-clearing checks.

Automated static-analysis cleanup: a detekt-fix workflow that proves a change is behavior-neutral by token-level diff before committing; cleared lint across 35 repo MRs without suppressions or baselines, enforced by a pre-push gate.

Added guardrails to keep automation safe at team scale: stale-ticket read guard before commenting, skip rules for cancelled / non-actionable tickets, evidence thresholds before challenging QC expectations or design, and CI gates that block false-pass builds.

Produced self-test handover packages (business flow -> code mapping, step-by-step scenarios, test data) and performance RCA reports, so members who don't know the domain can verify fixes quickly before hand-off to QC.
